_gate.rule:
(decided before running): a level spec replaces "yoy" if its mean PRE MAE
across horizons is no more than 5% above yoy's and it is not worse at more than
one horizon by over 10%. The level specs are preferred on economics (receipts
proportional to the GDP level), so the gate asks only that fit is not given up.
Among passing specs, the lower PRE mean wins. OOS is reported, never selected on.

reasons.receipts: CBO's revenues include tariff receipts at the rates in force when it forecast and its own income and payroll tax projections; ours hold revenues' share of GDP moving back toward its mean.
reasons.primary: Definitions: ours exclude intragovernmental interest offsets that CBO nets in outlays; the forecast part is CBO's mandatory spending growth (Social Security, Medicare) above prices.
reasons.interest: Ours is gross interest on Treasury debt from our book; CBO's is net interest.

uk.label: OBR EFO October 2026
uk.source: OBR EFO October 2026, Tables A.5, A.7 and A.9

reasons.receipts: The OBR has receipts rising from 40.1% of GDP in 2025-26 to 42.7% by 2029-30. Our model gives income tax + NICs a frozen-threshold earnings elasticity of 1.3 through FY 2027-28 (OBR EFO Oct 2026 para 4.14); from FY 2028-29 thresholds would have indexed under prior law so that component returns to unit elasticity and Budget 2025's extension to April 2031 sits only in the policy line. Remaining gap: capital taxes, corporation tax and non-dom one-offs.
reasons.primary: The OBR's welfare (triple lock, health and disability caseloads) and other AME grow faster than prices; our model grows spending with prices (departmental plans are in our policy line).
reasons.interest: Ours is gross central government interest from our bond-by-bond book at today's curve; the OBR's is net of the Bank of England's APF.
